title: Zé Roberto announces retirement from women's volleyball national team in 2028
seoTitle: Zé Roberto to retire from Brazil women's volleyball in.
subtitle: The three-time Olympic champion coach reveals who might take over after the Los Angeles Olympics
excerpt: Zé Roberto Guimarães confirmed he will leave the women's national volleyball team after the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In an exclusive interview with Lance!, Zé Roberto Guimarães confirmed he will leave the women's national volleyball team after the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. The coach, who has led the team since 2003, stated that the decision to make way for new leadership is necessary to maintain the legacy he built.

Why the Topic is Trending Now

The announcement came shortly after the national team's transition plans were revealed, generating significant interest among fans and volleyball specialists. The news was published on October 13th, a day when the sports press focused interviews on the team's future.

Zé Roberto's Legacy with the Women's National Team

The coach boasts an impressive resume: gold medals at the Beijing 2008 and London 2012 Olympics, in addition to victories in world championships. He stated that the women's national team has been built with the help of several coaches over the years, but that the project's continuity depends on a well-planned succession.

Paulo Coco, the Candidate to Take Over

Zé Roberto named Paulo Coco, his assistant, as the most suitable candidate to take over. He emphasized that Coco has worked with him for many years and contributed to the podium finishes achieved in recent years. The assistant also served as head coach for the staff at LOVB Miami, an experience praised by the coach.

How the Transition Will Occur

The coach stated that the confederation will be responsible for the final decision, but that he would like to participate in the selection. He believes that the new leadership must maintain the winning culture that Brazil has developed in women's volleyball.

Zé Roberto's Future Outside the National Team

Despite leaving the team, Zé Roberto does not intend to exit the sports world. He stated that he will remain involved in volleyball development projects, especially the Barueri project, which he manages with his family.

Conclusion

Zé Roberto's decision to retire after 2028 marks the end of an era of achievements for Brazilian volleyball. The choice of Paulo Coco as his successor could ensure the continuity of success on the international stage.
